summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY. Built and administered embedded Linux systems on NVIDIA Jetson and Raspberry Pi: a systemd-managed Jetson service with auto-restart, non-root isolation and static IP networking, plus multi-camera multiprocessing capture in Python. Wrote bare-metal embedded C firmware for ARM Cortex-M (STM32) with interrupt-driven UART, I2C and ADC, and resolved 11 integration failures across hardware and software.

Embedded Linux & Languages: systemd service management (unit files, auto-restart, non-root isolation)
Embedded / Firmware: ARM embedded hardware development (STM32 Cortex-M bare-metal C)

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Deployed the Jetson-side arm bridge as a systemd service (Type=simple, auto-restart with backoff, non-root user/group isolation, environment-file-based config) with static IP networking for reliable multi-device WebSocket registration; configured XRDP for remote desktop administration of the headless Jetson.
Built a LeRobot-structured data collection pipeline using multiprocessing for multi-camera frame capture.
Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end voice-to-picked latency.

Built a voice-controlled, vision-guided robotic pick-and-place system on a Jetson+Arduino controller with a Flask-SocketIO edge server over a unified WebSocket fabric; integrated TensorRT-optimized YOLO (5.2× speedup: 56.7→10.9 ms) and dual VL53L0X ToF sensors via a TCA9548A I2C mux.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built a Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to STM32 over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.
Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing.

projects.name: SLM Compression and Benchmarking for Edge Deployment
bullets: Reduced GPU memory footprint by ~55% via 8-bit quantization (bitsandbytes LLM.int8()) on TinyLlama 1.1B; profiled peak VRAM and inference latency across prompt types using pynvml and psutil.
